description:
Issue a tax or ordinary invoice. This is a real financial document: it takes the next sequential number, computes VAT, generates the ZATCA QR code and posts to the general ledger. It cannot be edited afterwards — correct it with a credit note. Confirm the amounts with the user before calling.

Use taxTreatment "tax" for a VAT-registered business, "ordinary" for one that is not registered. Use type "simplified" for individuals, "standard" for businesses (which requires the buyer's VAT number).

buyer.description: Who the invoice is for. Required for a standard (B2B) invoice, where name and vatNumber must both be present.

address.description: Buyer's address as it should appear on the invoice.

email.description: Buyer's email, used if the invoice is sent.

vatNumber.description: Buyer's 15-digit Saudi VAT number, required on a standard (B2B) invoice.

lines.description: The invoice lines. At least one. Amounts are in Saudi riyals unless the org bills in another currency.

description.description: What is being charged for, as it should read on the invoice.

unitPrice.description: Price for one unit, before VAT unless pricesIncludeVat is true.

notes.description: Free text printed on the invoice, visible to the buyer.

pricesIncludeVat.description: True when each line unitPrice already contains VAT, so it is divided out rather than added on.

taxTreatment.description: "tax" for a VAT invoice from a VAT-registered seller, "ordinary" when the seller is not VAT registered. An ordinary invoice carries no VAT and no QR code.

type.description: ZATCA document type: "simplified" for a sale to an individual (B2C), "standard" for a sale to a business (B2B), which requires the buyer's name and VAT number.

name: fawtar_create_invoice
title: Issue an invoice
